steps.intent: France’s objective is to renew MINUSCA with a robust, protection-focused mandate that preserves APPR centrality, supports state authority and SSR, and strengthens accountability and human rights compliance. The main difficulties will be balancing firm language on mercenaries, human rights due diligence and the 2025 electoral process with Russian and CAR Government sensitivities, while keeping the text broad enough to secure at least nine votes and avoid a veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the penholder’s text and can support the renewal of MINUSCA. We ask that the strategic review in OP12 be conducted in consultation with the CAR Government, the African Union, ECCAS and the ICGLR, and that OP7 reaffirm the CAR authorities’ primary responsibility for the electoral process and the need for MINUSCA support to be provided upon request and in full respect for CAR sovereignty. These changes reinforce African ownership, consent and non-interference.
messages.China: China appreciates France’s penholder role and supports the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. To strengthen CAR ownership and the basic peacekeeping principle of host-State consent, China requests that operational support and the strategic review be conducted in close consultation with the CAR Government, with the review aligned with the CAR’s national development strategy. China can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the renewal of MINUSCA and welcomes France’s balanced draft. Our red line is that UN support to CAR security forces must remain fully conditioned on the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, including in joint operations. We also ask for targeted language protecting civic space in the electoral context and for climate-related security risks to be included in reporting.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the renewal of MINUSCA's mandate and the balanced thrust of the French draft. We would like the text to make clearer that international support to the CAR, including bilateral support, must respect the country's sovereignty and Charter principles, and that UN support to security forces is strictly conditional on HRDDP compliance. We also ask for a standard call for full cooperation with the ICC and the Special Criminal Court.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate and the draft’s strong emphasis on protection of civilians, the APPR and accountability. We request stronger language on transparent and accountable coordination of all international security support, including private military contractors, consistent with human rights due diligence. We also ask that reporting explicitly cover climate-related security risks and food insecurity, which are central to Guyana’s priorities.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate and the priority tasks set out in the French draft. As a major troop- and police-contributing country, Pakistan asks the penholder to strengthen OP5 on accountability for attacks against peacekeepers and to add a new OP on regular TCC/PCC consultations and tripartite mechanisms with the CAR Government before any reconfiguration or drawdown. We also stress that robust action must remain within the basic principles of peacekeeping, including host-State consent and close coordination with national authorities.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate and the thrust of the French text. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 with accountability for attacks on peacekeepers, to reinforce OP8 with vetting and follow-up under the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and to add climate-related security risk reporting in OP12. These changes are consistent with Panama’s priorities on protection of civilians, human rights and the climate-security nexus.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate and the robust, people-centred orientation of the draft. We would ask the penholder to add explicit language on accountability for attacks against United Nations and humanitarian personnel and to strengthen Human Rights Due Diligence Policy conditionality for support to CAR security forces. We are flexible on wording and ready to join consensus.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation can support the renewal of MINUSCA, but we cannot accept the positive reference to the International Criminal Court or its 24 July 2025 judgments; that clause must be deleted. We also ask that the text avoid singling out so-called 'mercenaries' and instead refer to violations by all parties, while respecting the CAR Government's sovereign choices in security cooperation. We are ready to engage constructively on this basis.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of MINUSCA's mandate and the draft's strong focus on protection of civilians, the peace process and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP12 by ensuring the strategic review is conducted in consultation with troop- and police-contributing countries and the CAR authorities, and by including reporting on WPS, youth and climate-related security risks. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks France for the balanced renewal text and supports its swift adoption. We would like to see the climate-related risk assessment language restored in line with resolution 2759, stronger condemnation of mercenary activities and disinformation against MINUSCA, and clearer guarantees for a safe enabling environment for political opposition, civil society and journalists ahead of the elections. We also ask that reporting include the Women, Peace and Security agenda and climate-related security risks.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of MINUSCA and the broad thrust of the French draft. We ask the penholder to strengthen explicit African ownership through the AU, ECCAS and ICGLR, add operational language on cross-border threats and arms trafficking, and ensure TCC/PCC consultation in the strategic review. These are constructive, non-blocking changes aimed at improving implementation and regional coherence.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports a timely renewal of MINUSCA's mandate and thanks France for a strong draft. To strengthen the text, we ask that PP4 restore agreed responsibility-to-protect language and that OP5 explicitly address the night flight restrictions and full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement. We also seek clear condemnation of all violations and abuses, including by Government forces and their security partners, with accountability through the Special Criminal Court and national authorities.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing MINUSCA's mandate, but we need the Council to send a clear message on the Wagner Group and other foreign-backed mercenaries, whose activities undermine CAR sovereignty and stability. We also insist on explicit language on full implementation of the status-of-forces agreement, including lifting night-flight restrictions, and on compliance with the CAR sanctions regime. We can support the text with these changes and look forward to working with France on compromise language.

replies.China: partially accepted: host-State consultations included, but national development strategy is taken into account rather than binding alignment
replies.Greece: partially accepted: SCC/national judicial cooperation included but ICC reference omitted to preserve consensus
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: positive ICC judgment reference removed, but generic mercenaries language retained
replies.United States of America: partially accepted: sanctions, SOFA and night-flight language included; Wagner not named and drawdown language softened

steps.summary: The revised text preserves a robust MINUSCA mandate while adding host-State consultation, stronger HRDDP conditionality, sanctions compliance, and climate/WPS reporting. It removes the positive ICC judgment reference and avoids naming the Wagner Group, aiming to forestall a Russian veto while retaining broad support. Russia may abstain over the remaining mercenaries language, but the draft is expected to secure the required votes.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the incorporation of the A3+ requests, notably African leadership and ownership in the peace process, respect for CAR sovereignty in electoral support, and inclusive consultation for the strategic review. The text reflects a balanced, CAR-owned and African-led approach consistent with MINUSCA’s mandate and the principle of non-interference. Algeria therefore supports the current draft and encourages the Council to adopt it unanimously.
messages.China: China supports the current text and will vote in favour of the renewal of MINUSCA's mandate. We appreciate that the penholder has incorporated host-State consultation and taken into account the CAR's national development strategy, which are essential for the Mission's effectiveness and for respecting the country's sovereignty. China hopes MINUSCA will work closely with the CAR Government to implement the APPR and protect civilians. We continue to believe the sanctions regime should be adjusted in light of progress, but this does not prevent our support for the mandate renewal.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on HRDDP conditionality, civic space, and climate-related security risk reporting. The text now reflects a balanced and credible mandate that prioritises protection of civilians, accountability and inclusive political processes. We support the draft as it stands and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft. We welcome the incorporation of the sovereignty and Charter language on coordination and the strengthened Human Rights Due Diligence Policy conditionality. While we would have preferred an explicit reference to the International Criminal Court alongside the Special Criminal Court, we accept the penholder’s consensus compromise and encourage robust implementation of MINUSCA’s protection and accountability tasks.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for accepting our earlier amendments on transparency, accountability, the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and reporting on climate-related security risks and food insecurity. We support the current text as balanced and consistent with Guyana’s priorities on sovereignty, civilian protection, women and youth participation, and African-led peace efforts. We encourage all Council members to join consensus and urge full implementation of the mandate.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for accepting our proposals on accountability for attacks against United Nations personnel and on systematic consultations with troop- and police-contributing countries, including on mandate implementation and drawdown. The revised text is balanced, upholds CAR sovereignty and African ownership, and provides a robust civilian-protection mandate while prioritizing peacekeeper safety. Pakistan supports the current text and will vote in favour.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the revised draft and the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. We welcome the incorporation of our earlier amendments on accountability for attacks against United Nations personnel, Human Rights Due Diligence Policy vetting, and climate-related security risk reporting. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and adopt the text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of our proposals on accountability and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy and supports the current text. We believe the draft sends a united message on protecting civilians, supporting the APPR and African-owned peace efforts, and ensuring accountability. We therefore join consensus and encourage robust implementation of MINUSCA’s mandate.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of MINUSCA and welcomes the removal of the ICC judgment reference. We cannot, however, accept PP8's explicit condemnation of CAR Government forces and their security partners or PP10's singling out of 'foreign-backed private military and security personnel'; these are unbalanced and politically motivated. We also ask for OP7 to be brought into line with our long-standing position on the arms embargo. With these changes, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current text as revised. We thank the penholder for accepting our proposals on consulting troop- and police-contributing countries and the CAR authorities in the strategic review, and on reporting on WPS/YPS and climate-related security risks. The text preserves African ownership and a robust, realistic MINUSCA mandate, and we encourage all members to unite behind it.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the penholder for the inclusive process and for incorporating our earlier suggestions on protection of civilians, accountability, the Women, Peace and Security agenda, and climate-related security risks. We believe the revised text strikes the right balance and includes the necessary safeguards, notably HRDDP conditionality and support for the Special Criminal Court. Slovenia therefore supports the current draft and looks forward to its adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia welcomes the incorporation of its earlier requests on African ownership, cross-border coordination and consultation with troop- and police-contributing countries. We support the text in its current form and encourage the Council to adopt it by consensus.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks France for incorporating our earlier requests on the responsibility to protect, the Status of Forces Agreement and night-flight restrictions, and on accountability for violations by all parties, including Government forces and their security partners. We support the revised text as a balanced and robust renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate, with protection of civilians, human rights due diligence, humanitarian access and accountability at its core. We encourage all Council members to support it.
messages.United States of America: We welcome the inclusion of the sanctions, SOFA and night-flight language, and we support the overall renewal of MINUSCA. We continue to believe the Council should explicitly name the Wagner Group in PP8 rather than rely only on the phrase 'foreign-backed private military and security personnel,' given its documented abuses and destabilizing role. With that change, we are prepared to support the text.

replies.Russian Federation: accepted: PP8, PP10 and OP7 revised as requested
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: accepted: no further changes requested; earlier amendments retained
replies.United States of America: rejected: explicit naming of the Wagner Group not added; generic mercenaries language retained to preserve consensus

steps.summary: France revised the draft to accommodate Russia's red lines by removing language singling out Government forces and security partners, and foreign-backed private military personnel, while retaining accountability for all parties and generic mercenaries language. Russia's OP7 sanctions language was accepted, but the US request to name the Wagner Group was rejected to maintain consensus and avoid a Russian veto. The draft is expected to be adopted with 14 votes in favour and one abstention.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported MINUSCA’s stabilization role and the APPR/Luanda process, and the draft reflects its priorities on sovereignty, African ownership, civilian protection, and accountability without requiring changes.
reasons.China: China supported the draft in the last negotiation round with no requested changes, consistent with its support for MINUSCA mandate renewal and CAR-owned peace and stability efforts. As a routine renewal that respects CAR sovereignty and includes sanctions review language, China would vote in favour.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports MINUSCA’s mandate renewal and the resolution’s focus on civilian protection, human rights due diligence, accountability and humanitarian access. The draft aligns with Denmark’s multilateral and human rights priorities, so we vote in favour.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and a strong supporter of MINUSCA; the draft reflects its priorities on protection, accountability and human rights. As a permanent member, France would vote in favour and encourage consensus.
reasons.Greece: Greece strongly supports UN peacekeeping and a rules-based multilateral response, so it backs the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate with human rights safeguards and respect for CAR sovereignty. No national interest or alliance consideration in this file suggests abstention or opposition.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supported the prior MINUSCA mandate renewal and has no outstanding changes; the draft aligns with its emphasis on sovereignty, civilian protection, African-led peace processes and accountability.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan was recorded as supporting the draft and had no requested changes; as an elected member with a strong UN peacekeeping tradition, it would vote yes while emphasising consent, sovereignty and African ownership.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports peacekeeping mandates that prioritize civilian protection and accountability, and the draft reflects its key concerns on HRDDP and sovereignty.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported MINUSCA and previously voted in favour of the mandate renewal; the draft aligns with its emphasis on peacekeeping, protection of civilians, accountability and sovereignty. No changes were requested and the delegation indicated support in the last negotiation round.
reasons.Russian Federation: The penholder accepted Russia's red-line changes on balanced condemnations and a generic mercenaries reference, and OP7 now reflects Russia's requested sanctions-review language. Russia therefore supports extending MINUSCA while reiterating its long-standing calls for respecting CAR sovereignty and reviewing the arms embargo.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently supports MINUSCA’s mandate and peacekeeping in Africa, and the draft aligns with its emphasis on African-led peace efforts, civilian protection and accountability. No changes were requested, so it votes in favour and explains its support.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia is a consistent supporter of MINUSCA renewals and prioritizes protection of civilians, human rights compliance, accountability and inclusive peace processes, matching its last-round support and no requested changes.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia’s position in the last negotiation round was support and the draft aligns with its emphasis on African ownership, sovereignty and UN peacekeeping. It would vote in favour and use a brief explanation of vote to underline those priorities.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports MINUSCA’s renewal and the draft reflects key UK priorities: civilian protection, accountability, R2P language, freedom of movement and HRDDP compliance. Voting in favour is consistent with the UK’s previous votes and stated positions on this agenda item.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports renewing MINUSCA’s mandate despite the rejected request to name the Wagner Group, while using the explanation of vote to register that concern and highlight human rights and accountability priorities.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We believe the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate is essential to supporting the protection of civilians, the implementation of the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation, and the Luanda roadmap. At the same time, we stress that international support must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic and must be coordinated in a manner that reinforces African ownership and the primacy of the CAR Government’s responsibility for peace, reconciliation and stabilization.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We thank France for its penholdership and welcome the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. Denmark firmly supports MINUSCA’s protection-of-civilians role and a robust, proactive posture where civilians are at risk. We welcome the emphasis on accountability, the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and the protection of children and survivors of conflict-related sexual violence. Support to national defence and security forces must remain strictly conditional on full compliance with human rights and international humanitarian law. The humanitarian situation is dire, and all parties must ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We call on the CAR Government and all armed groups to cooperate fully with MINUSCA and to engage in an inclusive, CAR-owned peace process with the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. Denmark remains concerned by the continued violence, including by armed groups and mercenaries, and underscores the need for coherent, transparent and accountable international support to the CAR.
before.France: France will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council, which it has had the honour to present. The renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate until 15 November 2026 is essential. The resolution maintains a robust mandate focused on the protection of civilians, support for the peace process and the APPR, the extension of State authority, security sector reform, human rights and the fight against impunity, and humanitarian access. We stress that support to the Central African defence and security forces must remain strictly conditional on full respect for international humanitarian law, human rights law and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. France calls on all Council members to support this text unanimously, in the interest of the Central African people and of the stability of the region.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate as essential to the protection of civilians, the preservation of the ceasefire architecture, and the extension of State authority in the Central African Republic. Greece underlines the importance of full respect for international humanitarian law and human rights, including the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, and of accountability for all violations. We also stress that international support must remain coherent, transparent and fully respectful of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic, with a leading role for African partners and the CAR Government.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for the balanced and comprehensive text. We support the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate, with a clear focus on protection of civilians, robust peacekeeping, support for the APPR and African-led peace efforts, extension of State authority, accountability through the Special Criminal Court, and safe humanitarian access. We underscore the importance of full respect for the CAR’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and we will vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Pakistan: Mr. President, Pakistan thanks the penholder for its efforts and the inclusive consultations that have produced this draft. Pakistan will vote in favour of the resolution. We support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate, particularly its civilian protection role, support for the APPR and the peace process, extension of State authority, security sector reform, humanitarian access and accountability. At the same time, Pakistan stresses that MINUSCA must act in full accordance with the basic principles of peacekeeping—consent of the parties, impartiality, and non-use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate—and in close coordination with the Government of the Central African Republic. We underline the centrality of CAR ownership and African-led and African-owned solutions, including the African Union, ECCAS and the ICGLR, and we call on all partners to respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic. We also stress the importance of predictable resources, the safety and security of peacekeepers, and full cooperation by the host authorities and all parties with the Mission.
before.Panama: Mr. President, Panama votes in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate because the protection of civilians, the promotion of human rights, the fight against impunity and unhindered humanitarian access remain indispensable. We stress that all United Nations support to the CAR defence and security forces must be strictly conditional on full compliance with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Panama condemns all violence against civilians and peacekeepers, including by armed groups and mercenaries, and calls on all parties to respect the APPR and to cooperate fully with MINUSCA. We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic.
before.Republic of Korea: Thank you, Mr./Madam President. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate and its priority tasks, especially the protection of civilians, good offices in support of the APPR and African-led peace efforts, and support for State authority, security sector reform and the rule of law. We underscore the importance of full implementation of the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, accountability for violations and abuses, and safe, timely and unhindered humanitarian access. We also stress that international support to the CAR, including security assistance, must be transparent, coordinated and fully respectful of the CAR’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We call on all parties to cease attacks against peacekeepers and civilians and to cooperate fully with MINUSCA. The Republic of Korea remains committed to supporting the peace process and the people of the Central African Republic.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We note that the penholder has taken into account our fundamental concerns: the text commends accountability in a balanced manner without singling out Government forces and their partners, its reference to mercenaries is generic, and it provides for keeping the sanctions measures under review in light of the CAR Government’s requests and improved conditions on the ground. We support the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate, including protection of civilians and support for the peace process. At the same time, we stress that the Central African Republic bears primary responsibility for its security and that international support must fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the country, as well as national ownership and the principle of African solutions to African problems. We also reiterate that the sanctions regime, above all the arms embargo, must not obstruct Bangui’s efforts to ensure security and combat illegal armed groups.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr President. Sierra Leone will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate and its emphasis on protecting civilians, supporting the political process and extending State authority. Sierra Leone underscores the importance of African ownership and close coordination with the African Union, ECCAS and the ICGLR. We call on the CAR Government and all armed groups to cooperate fully with MINUSCA, ensure humanitarian access, protect civilians and end impunity. All international support, including joint operations, must comply strictly with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy.
before.Slovenia: Thank you, Mr. President. Slovenia will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate and its priority tasks, in particular the protection of civilians, support for the APPR and the ICGLR roadmap, and the extension of State authority. We stress that United Nations support to the CAR defence and security forces must remain strictly conditional on full compliance with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. Accountability remains essential; we support the Special Criminal Court and call on all States to cooperate with it. The full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth, and the protection of children, are central to a sustainable political solution. We also underscore the need for unhindered humanitarian access and the safety of peacekeepers and humanitarian personnel. Slovenia remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic and to a CAR-owned, African-led peace process. We thank France for its work as penholder.
before.Somalia: Thank you, Mr. President. Somalia votes in favour of this resolution. As an African member of this Council, we strongly support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate, including its civilian-protection, peace-process and State-authority tasks, and we reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic. We stress the central role of the African Union and regional organizations, the inclusive implementation of the APPR, accountability for violations, and unhindered humanitarian access. Somalia remains committed to supporting African-led solutions to African peace and security challenges.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank France for its work as penholder and welcome the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate. MINUSCA continues to play an essential role in protecting civilians, supporting the peace process and helping the CAR authorities extend State authority. We welcome the retention of language affirming the CAR Government’s responsibility to protect civilians from genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity, and the emphasis on accountability, including through the Special Criminal Court. We also stress the importance of full implementation of the Status of Forces Agreement, including the lifting of restrictions on night flights, and of strict compliance with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. The United Kingdom remains concerned by continued violence by armed groups and by reports of abuses by all parties, including Government forces and their security partners. We support this renewal and will continue to follow the situation closely.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We strongly support the renewal of MINUSCA’s mandate and its vital work to protect civilians, support the peace process, strengthen State authority, and help create the conditions for accountable, transparent and inclusive governance in the Central African Republic. We welcome the resolution’s emphasis on peacekeeper safety, full implementation of the Status of Forces Agreement, the lifting of restrictions on night flights, compliance with the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy, the fight against impunity, and the protection of children and victims of conflict-related sexual violence. We remain concerned, however, that the Council has again declined to name the Wagner Group explicitly. The Wagner Group and other foreign-backed private military personnel have committed abuses, undermined stability, and exploited the country’s resources. Generic language is insufficient. The United States will continue to insist on accountability and on ensuring that international support to the CAR is transparent, coordinated, and fully consistent with human rights and humanitarian law. We nonetheless vote in favour because MINUSCA’s mandate is essential and the Central African people deserve the Council’s continued support.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted renewing the mandate of MINUSCA. We thank France for its work as penholder and welcome the constructive efforts of Council members.

China supports MINUSCA in continuing to play an active role in protecting civilians, supporting the political process, extending State authority and helping the Central African Republic strengthen its security capacity. We hope the renewal will help create favourable conditions for the smooth conduct of the country’s political process and elections.

At the same time, China stresses that MINUSCA should strictly abide by its mandate and the basic principles of peacekeeping, including consent of the parties, impartiality and non-use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate. It should fully respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic, strengthen communication and coordination with the CAR Government, and support CAR-owned and African-led solutions.

The international community should provide support in a coherent, transparent and effective manner and avoid interfering in the internal affairs of the CAR. China also believes that sanctions measures should be reviewed and adjusted in light of progress on the ground and the legitimate concerns of the CAR Government, so as to avoid affecting the country’s efforts to maintain security and stability.

China will continue to support the peace, stability and development of the Central African Republic.
after.France: France welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing MINUSCA’s mandate until 15 November 2026. This unanimity is important: MINUSCA operates in a difficult environment, and it needs the full support of the Security Council. The text preserves a robust mandate centred on the protection of civilians, support for the APPR and the Luanda roadmap, the extension of State authority, security sector reform, human rights and humanitarian access. France stresses that United Nations support to the Central African defence and security forces must remain strictly conditional on full compliance with international humanitarian law, human rights law and the Human Rights Due Diligence Policy. We regret that the Council did not explicitly name the Wagner Group, whose activities and abuses continue to threaten civilians and stability in the Central African Republic. Accountability, including through the Special Criminal Court, and full implementation of the Status of Forces Agreement, including the lifting of restrictions on night flights, remain essential. France will continue to work with the Central African authorities, African partners and all Council members in support of a CAR-owned political process and lasting peace.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution and welcomes its adoption. We support the extension of MINUSCA’s mandate, above all its role in protecting civilians and supporting the CAR-owned political process. At the same time, we note that the text as adopted is the result of difficult compromise. It does not contain references to the International Criminal Court, whose politicisation and double standards we have repeatedly rejected, and it does not single out the Russian Federation or its lawful bilateral co-operation with the Central African Republic.

We stress that the primary responsibility for security, peace and reconciliation in the CAR lies with the CAR Government. MINUSCA and all international partners must act with full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Central African Republic, with the consent and close co-ordination of the national authorities. International support, including the training and capacity-building of the CAR defence and security forces, must not be turned into a mechanism of political pressure or a bureaucratic obstacle to legitimate co-operation.

We also note that the reference in the text to mercenaries is generic. Any attempt to use such language for targeted attacks against legitimate military and technical co-operation with the CAR is unacceptable and will be firmly opposed. The fight against impunity must be balanced and impartial; it must not be used selectively against Government forces or their partners. National courts and national institutions have the primary role in ensuring accountability.

The Russian Federation reiterates that the sanctions regime, and in particular the arms embargo, has outlived its usefulness and undermines Bangui’s ability to combat illegal armed groups. We will continue to press for its lifting and for a realistic review of the sanctions measures in light of the CAR Government’s requests and the improvements on the ground. We call on all armed groups to cease violence and on all international partners to co-ordinate their support for the APPR and the Luanda roadmap without imposing external agendas.
